literature.headline_zh: 埃博拉病毒类群本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期埃博拉病毒类群研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 第一位参与者于2026年7月24日收到了ChAdOx1 BDBV 疫苗,标志着一期试验的启动。所提供的证据中没有报告不良事件或免疫原性数据。 [10.1080/23744235.2026.2717159]
该研究报告称,扎伊尔埃博拉病毒对 GeneXpert 平台的过度依赖极大地导致了 2026 年本迪布焦埃博拉病毒 暴发 期间的延迟检测。它还强调需要更广泛的诊断工具和综合治理框架。 [10.1016/j.ijid.2026.109065]
所有 TaqMan 格式在各种仪器和试剂类型中均实现了每个反应 5 个拷贝的 95% 检测限,而 SYBR Green 测定则实现了每个反应 50 个拷贝的 95% 检测限。 [10.64898/2026.08.17.26360605]
该研究报告称,自乌干达宣布 暴发 结束以来,尽管刚果民主共和国正在进行 传播,但开发 疫苗、治疗 和本迪布焦埃博拉病毒诊断方法的研究工作已经加速。 [10.1016/j.lanmic.2026.101524]
创建证据图是为了提供有关丝状病毒(包括本迪布焦病毒)的文献的全面概述,并被设计为可以定期更新以保持其相关性的动态资源。 [10.1038/s41590-026-02623-2]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The first participant received the ChAdOx1 BDBV vaccine on July 24, 2026, marking the initiation of the Phase I trial. No adverse events or immunogenicity data are reported in the provided evidence. [10.1080/23744235.2026.2717159]

The study reports that the over-reliance on GeneXpert platforms for Zaire ebolavirus contributed significantly to delayed detection during the 2026 Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak. It also highlights the need for broader diagnostic tools and integrated governance frameworks. [10.1016/j.ijid.2026.109065]

All TaqMan formats achieved a 95% limit of detection of 5 copies per reaction across instruments and reagent types, while the SYBR Green assay achieved a 95% limit of detection of 50 copies per reaction. [10.64898/2026.08.17.26360605]

The study reported that research efforts to develop vaccines, treatments, and diagnostics against the Bundibugyo ebolavirus have accelerated since Uganda declared the outbreak over, despite the ongoing transmission in DR Congo. [10.1016/j.lanmic.2026.101524]

The evidence map was created to provide a comprehensive overview of the literature on filoviruses, including the Bundibugyo virus, and was designed to be a dynamic resource that can be updated regularly to maintain its relevance. [10.1038/s41590-026-02623-2]

papers.title_original: The first Bundibugyo virus vaccine trial: from first-in-human testing to outbreak readiness.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the urgent need for a vaccine against Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), an emerging orthoebolavirus causing severe hemorrhagic fever in humans. Prior to this trial, no BDBV-specific vaccine had been tested in humans, creating a critical knowledge gap in outbreak preparedness.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A Phase I clinical trial was conducted in Burundi (BD-Ebov) starting July 24, 2026, using the ChAdOx1 BDBV vaccine candidate. The study enrolled human participants to evaluate safety and immunogenicity, with no comparator group described in the provided evidence.
analysis.methods: The trial administered the ChAdOx1 BDBV vaccine via intramuscular injection to the first participant. Methods focused on initial safety assessment and immune response monitoring, though detailed protocols and statistical analyses are not specified in the evidence.
analysis.main_results: The first participant received the ChAdOx1 BDBV vaccine on July 24, 2026, marking the initiation of the Phase I trial. No adverse events or immunogenicity data are reported in the provided evidence.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors highlighted this as the first human trial of a BDBV-specific vaccine, establishing a foundation for future efficacy studies. This represents a novel milestone in orthoebolavirus vaccine development, though mechanistic insights remain preliminary.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The trial provides critical early data for BDBV vaccine development, informing potential deployment strategies during outbreaks. It underscores the importance of rapid vaccine development for emerging pathogens with high mortality risk.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to a single participant's vaccination event, with no follow-up data or safety assessments reported. The study design's small sample size and lack of comparator groups restrict generalizability, warranting a low confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This Phase I trial marks the first human administration of a Bundibugyo virus (BDBV)-specific vaccine (ChAdOx1 BDBV) in Burundi on July 24, 2026. papers.title: Governance Frameworks, Not Just Products: Overcoming Surveillance Blind Spots in the 2026 Bundibugyo Virus Outbreak.
papers.abstract: To the Editor— We read with great interest the Editorial by Haider et al. [1], which highlights critical diagnostic limitations during the 2026 Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. We agree that over-reliance on GeneXpert platforms designed primarily for Zaire ebolavirus contributed significantly to delayed detection. While the authors rightly call for pan-ebolavirus molecular assays, we argue that better tools alone will not prevent future failures without governance frameworks that integrate them into routine clinical algorithms.

papers.title: Ebola Virus Disease: Hematologic Insights and Public Health Innovations- A Narrative Review
papers.abstract: Ebola virus disease remains a formidable zoonotic infection marked by severe hematologic disturbances and high case fatality. Beyond its well-known hemorrhagic manifestations, EVD is characterized by complex coagulopathy, platelet dysfunction, endothelial injury, and immune dysregulation, which together drive disease severity and poor outcomes. This narrative review highlights the hematologic mechanisms underlying EVD pathogenesis, including disseminated intravascular coagulation, cytokine-driven vascular leakage, and bone marrow suppression, while discussing their clinical and diagnostic implications. In parallel, we examine recent public health innovations—from rapid diagnostics and monoclonal antibody therapies to ring vaccination and AI-assisted surveillance—that have transformed outbreak preparedness and response. By integrating hematologic insights with advances in public health interventions, this review underscores the critical need for multidisciplinary strategies to reduce mortality, improve patient management, and prevent future Ebola outbreaks

In parallel, we examine recent public health innovations—from rapid diagnostics and monoclonal antibody therapies to ring vaccination and AI-assisted surveillance—that have transformed outbreak preparedness and response. By integrating hematologic insights with advances in public health interventions, this review underscores the critical need for multidisciplinary strategies to reduce mortality, improve patient management, and prevent future Ebola outbreaks

papers.title: Renewed Confirmed-Case Reporting in Health Zones After 21 Days Without a Newly Attributed Case During the 2026 Bundibugyo Virus Disease Outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: Implications for Health-Zone Surveillance and Response
papers.abstract: Background: During the geographically dispersed 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), 21 days without a newly attributed confirmed case may inform health-zone surveillance and resource-allocation decisions while transmission continues elsewhere. However, the frequency and timing of renewed confirmed-case reporting after this interval have not been quantified. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted among health zones affected by the 2026 BVD outbreak in the DRC. The primary data source was the national situation-report series, triangulated with World Health Organization weekly reports. Health zones that completed 21 days without a newly attributed confirmed case by 2 August 2026 entered the cohort. The observed recurrence proportion, incidence per 100 zone-days and Kaplan-Meier time to recurrence were estimated. Spatial adjacency to zones with reported confirmed-case activity during the 21 days before each focal health zone completed the interval was described. Results: Seventeen of 51 affected health zones completed the 21-day interval. Ten subsequently reported recurrence and seven were right-censored, giving an observed recurrence proportion of 58.8% (95% exact confidence interval 32.9% to 81.6%). The incidence was 2.83 recurrences per 100 zone-days (95% confidence interval 1.36 to 5.21). The estimated cumulative probability of recurrence was 20.0% by day 7, 41.3% by day 14, 48.7% by day 21 and 56.0% by day 28; median recurrence-free time was 22 days. All recurrent health zones and five of seven censored zones shared a boundary with a zone that had reported confirmed-case activity during the 21 days before threshold crossing. Aggregate reports could not distinguish persistent undetected transmission, reintroduction, delayed confirmation or retrospective attribution. Conclusions: Completion of 21 days without a newly attributed confirmed case was frequently followed by reported recurrence. The interval should not be used as a stand-alone trigger for substantial surveillance de-escalation. Decisions should also consider subsequent observation time, nearby case activity, surveillance performance and unresolved laboratory or reporting constraints.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 在刚果民主共和国 (DRC) 发生地理分散的 2026 年本迪布焦病毒病 (BVD) 暴发 期间,如果 21 天没有新确诊病例,可能会影响卫生区 监测 和资源分配决策,而 传播 会在其他地方继续传播。然而,在此间隔之后重新报告确诊病例的频率和时间尚未量化。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在刚果民主共和国受 2026 年 BVD 暴发 影响的卫生区中进行了一项回顾性 队列研究 研究。截至 2026 年 8 月 2 日,连续 21 天没有新增确诊病例的卫生区进入 队列研究。
elements_zh.methods: 主要数据来源是国家形势报告系列,与世界卫生组织每周报告进行三角测量。估计观察到的复发比例、每 100 个区域日的 发病率 和 Kaplan-Meier 复发时间。
elements_zh.main_results: 51 个受影响的卫生区中有 17 个完成了 21 天的间隔。随后有 10 例报告复发,7 例经过右删失,观察到的复发率为 58.8%(95% 准确置信区间为 32.9% 至 81.6%)。发病率 为每 100 个区域日 2.83 次复发(95% 置信区间为 1.36 至 5.21)。估计的累积复发概率在第7天时为20.0%,在第14天时为41.3%,在第21天时为48.7%,在第28天时为56.0%;中位无复发时间为 22 天。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在没有新确诊病例的 21 天后,经常会报告复发情况。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该间隔不应用作 监测 大幅降级的独立触发器。决策还应考虑后续观察时间、附近病例活动、监测 表现以及未解决的实验室或报告限制。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 汇总报告无法区分持续未检测到的 传播、重新引入、延迟确认或追溯归因。证据是温和的,因为该研究是基于汇总报告,并且没有考虑所有潜在的混杂因素。

Health zones that completed 21 days without a newly attributed confirmed case by 2 August 2026 entered the cohort. The observed recurrence proportion, incidence per 100 zone-days and Kaplan-Meier time to recurrence were estimated. Spatial adjacency to zones with reported confirmed-case activity during the 21 days before each focal health zone completed the interval was described. Results: Seventeen of 51 affected health zones completed the 21-day interval. Ten subsequently reported recurrence and seven were right-censored, giving an observed recurrence proportion of 58.8% (95% exact confidence interval 32.9% to 81.6%). The incidence was 2.83 recurrences per 100 zone-days (95% confidence interval 1.36 to 5.21). The estimated cumulative probability of recurrence was 20.0% by day 7, 41.3% by day 14, 48.7% by day 21 and 56.0% by day 28; median recurrence-free time was 22 days. All recurrent health zones and five of seven censored zones shared a boundary with a zone that had reported confirmed-case activity during the 21 days before threshold crossing. Aggregate reports could not distinguish persistent undetected transmission, reintroduction, delayed confirmation or retrospective attribution. Conclusions: Completion of 21 days without a newly attributed confirmed case was frequently followed by reported recurrence. The interval should not be used as a stand-alone trigger for substantial surveillance de-escalation. Decisions should also consider subsequent observation time, nearby case activity, surveillance performance and unresolved laboratory or reporting constraints.

papers.title: Configurationally Locked Ridaifen-B Analogs as Potent Ebola Virus Entry Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: In the face of emerging outbreaks, high mortality rates, and limited treatment options, Ebola virus (EBOV) disease poses a global public health threat, underscoring the need for effective therapies. The unique and critical role that EBOV glycoprotein (GP) plays in the viral life cycle makes it an attractive target for antiviral drug discovery. In this study, we report on the design, synthesis, and evaluation of a series of cyclized ridaifen-B-based inhibitors with enhanced antiviral activity and selectivity against EBOV. Several compounds exhibited nanomolar potency inhibiting EBOV-GP-mediated entry and submicromolar potency against Marburg virus entry. Site-directed mutagenesis indicated inhibitor binding at the EBOV GP1/GP2 fusion loop. The compounds displayed favorable in vitro pharmacokinetic parameters, which encouraged testing the in vivo rapid PK for hit compound 41. This study highlights the potential of 1,2-dihydronaphthalene and tetrahydronaphthalene derivatives as valuable leads for the development of potent antifiloviral agents targeting EBOV among other filoviruses.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Ebola virus disease poses a global public health threat due to its high mortality rates and limited treatment options, highlighting the need for effective therapies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study focused on the design, synthesis, and evaluation of cyclized ridaifen-B-based inhibitors targeting Ebola virus (EBOV) and related filoviruses, with an emphasis on antiviral activity and selectivity.
analysis.methods: The study involved the design and synthesis of a series of inhibitors, followed by their evaluation for antiviral activity against EBOV and related filoviruses through in vitro assays and site-directed mutagenesis to identify binding sites.
analysis.main_results: Several compounds showed nanomolar potency in inhibiting EBOV-GP-mediated entry and submicromolar potency against Marburg virus entry, with site-directed mutagenesis indicating inhibitor binding at the EBOV GP1/GP2 fusion loop.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that these compounds effectively target the EBOV glycoprotein, offering a novel approach for the development of potent antifiloviral agents.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide promising leads for the development of new antiviral therapies targeting EBOV, which could improve treatment options for Ebola virus disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro results, and further in vivo testing is needed to confirm efficacy and safety, which reduces the strength of the evidence to moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop potent antiviral agents targeting Ebola virus (EBOV) by designing and evaluating cyclized ridaifen-B-based inhibitors. The research highlighted the critical role of EBOV glycoprotein in the viral life cycle, making it an attractive target for drug discovery. Several compounds demonstrated nanomolar potency in inhibiting EBOV-GP-mediated entry, with site-directed mutagenesis indicating binding at the GP1/GP2 fusion loop. These findings suggest a novel approach for antifiloviral therapy, though the evidence is limited to in vitro results, reducing its strength to moderate. The study's results could inform future research into effective treatments for EBOV disease, but further in vivo testing is necessary to validate their therapeutic potential.

papers.full_text: nature immunology https://doi.org/10.1038/s41590-026-02623-2 Comment Accelerating the research response to the Bundibugyo virus emergency Mariah P. Csolle, Bronwyn A. Bailey, Yuna Chung, Tsharni R. Zazryn, Tari Turner, David S. Khoury & Miles P. Davenport In the context of a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, such as the Bundibugyo virus outbreak, the research community requires rapid access to information to guide an effective response. Evidence mapping brings together the available knowledge in a field into a single, organized resource, enabling researchers to rapidly identify priorities, gaps and opportunities for action. Immunology and microbiology research is crucial for combatting emerging infectious diseases. This was demonstrated during the COVID-19 pandemic when multiple vaccines, monoclonal antibody treatments and diagnostics were rapidly developed. The recent World Health Organization declaration of the Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) out- break in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo as a Public Health Emer- gency of International Concern (PHEIC) signals the need for researchers to once again respond dynamically to address a major health crisis. A challenge for immunologists in pivoting their research to a new area is knowing what has already been studied, and what the priorities are. Determining this requires investigators to have an overview of the lit- erature in the new field and to be confident that they have not missed a crucial study that might affect the direction or usefulness of their research. For individual investigators, this first step of gaining an over- view of the literature in a new field can require a substantial investment of time and act as a barrier to entry. But what if all the relevant literature on the topic had already been assembled and categorized? Evidence mapping aims to provide exactly that resource, enabling researchers to quickly find all the published research that is relevant to their work. Evidence mapping of filovirus research Evidence mapping is a systematic process for identifying relevant pub- lications in a specific area and categorizing them according to the evi- dence they provide (Fig. 1). The identified literature is then displayed as a two-dimensional map categorized according to population (for example, human, non-human primate (NHP), mouse), intervention (for example, vaccination, infection, treatment) and the outcomes measured (for example, antibody response, T cell response, outcome of infection). In contrast to traditional narrative literature reviews, an evidence map is specifically designed to provide a comprehensive and unbiased assembly of the available research, enabling researchers to conduct their own downstream analyses. The screening and mapping are performed independently by two reviewers to help ensure consist- ency, and the resulting maps can be disseminated as a resource for the wider research community. Maps can also be made ‘living’ by regular updates to keep them current. In 2024, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations (CEPI) identified the benefits of assembling the existing evidence on immunity and vaccination for their priority pathogens and providing this as an open resource for the health and medical communities. CEPI commissioned the development of evidence maps for three filoviruses, Marburg virus (MARV), Sudan virus (SUDV) and Ebola virus (EBOV), Check for updates Step 1: Systematically search databases Step 2: Screen title and abstracts Step 3: Screen full text and tag Step 4: Evidence map Search strategy: virus and (vaccine or model/assay) Potentially relevant → progress to full text BDBV vaccine efficacy Vaccination Mice Irrelevant: exclude BDBV vaccination in NHP Natural history of BDBV NHP Vaccine ELISA Human Infection Survival Categorize relevant articles Searchable map of all relevant studies Mouse studies Vaccine Infection outcomes Survival Viral load Treatment Infection challenge Fig. 1 | Mapping the immunological evidence for BDBV. Mapping involves systematically searching to identify the relevant literature, title and abstract screening to exclude irrelevant publications, and then reviewing the full texts to identify and categorize the relevant articles according to population, intervention and outcome reported. The final map enables rapid identification of all the available literature on a topic. ELISA, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. nature immunology Comment which were first produced in early 2025 and updated in September 2025. When the BDBV PHEIC was declared on 17 May 2026, the map- ping team rapidly assembled to make a map of the available evidence on BDBV vaccination and immunity. The resulting map was posted online on 21 May 2026 and updated on 22 July 2026 (available at https:// livingevidence.org.au/research-initiatives/about-feeva/evidence- maps/), and a preprint1 of the methods was published on 24 May 2026. Rapid production of an evidence map for BDBV was possible because of the established method for mapping filoviruses2 and the fact that only a small number of studies on BDBV immunity were available. A total of 49 publications were included on the original map (with an additional eight included in subsequent updates). By contrast, the equivalent maps for EBOV, MARV and SUDV include 857, 198 and 147 publications, respectively. Immunological findings for BDBV Immunity to filoviruses is thought to be largely mediated through antibodies to the surface glycoprotein. Two vaccines for EBOV have been approved, both based on the EBOV glycoprotein. Unfortunately, early evidence indicates limited cross-reactivity between the EBOV and BDBV glycoproteins, and it remains unclear whether EBOV vaccines will be effective against BDBV3. A number of animal studies have shown that BDBV glycoprotein-based vaccines and monoclonal antibodies to the BDBV glycoprotein can protect from severe infection4,5. Animal models of vaccination and infection were central to the approval of the Zabdeno/Mvabea vaccine for EBOV. These studies demonstrated that vaccine-induced antibody levels were associated with protection in a NHP model of EBOV infection6. By comparing the protective antibody levels in NHPs and the antibody levels induced after human vaccination, the investigators predicted that Zabdeno/Mvabea would be protective against EBOV infection in humans. Could a similar immunobridging approach be used in BDBV? Numerous animal models have been used for BDBV (including NHPs, mice, ferrets, pigs). However, only four stud- ies have looked at the association between vaccine-induced antibody levels and protection from infection in a cynomolgus macaque model of BDBV infection. Two studies analyzed prophylactic vaccination, with one study showing an association between antibody levels and protection7 but another study showing no association8. Similarly, two studies analyzed vaccination around the time of infection. While one study of vaccination 3 or 7 days before infection showed an associa- tion between antibody levels and viral levels (in a non-peer-reviewed preprint9), another study of post-exposure prophylaxis was dif- ficult to interpret because of the dynamic nature of early immune responses to vaccination and infection4. Further work on correlates of protection from BDBV infection in NHPs is clearly needed to support potential immunobridging. Understanding the immune response to natural BDBV infection — and whether natural immunity confers immunity to reinfection — could also inform the immune responses required for protection. However, there are only 10 studies of immune responses in survivors of BDBV (none of which measured T cell responses). In the case of EBOV, previous infection is thought to confer at least short-term immunity to reinfection (although cases of viral recrudescence have been reported; reviewed in ref. 10). However, it is not clear whether BDBV infection confers subsequent immunity to BDBV reinfection. Studies of the phenotype and durability of immune responses in survivors of BDBV infection — and whether or which of these responses confer protection from reinfection — are an important priority. Key to this is the develop- ment and dissemination of validated immunoassays for BDBV, which is critical to enable comparison of immune responses across natural history and vaccination studies, and to compare responses between animal models and human infection. Challenges and future directions While analysis of the current immunological literature on BDBV (through the evidence map) highlights the need for further charac- terization of immunity to BDBV, the challenges of performing such research should not be underestimated. The outbreak itself is occur- ring in a resource-limited setting affected by conflict. BDBV is highly pathogenic, meaning it must usually be handled in biosafety level 4 facilities, greatly reducing the number of laboratories that can perform such studies. However, the challenge of BDBV research also highlights the importance of using robust, validated and, ideally, standardized assays in those studies that are performed. Further, these studies should focus on the key gaps in BDBV knowledge that are most important for the public health response and for the development of vaccines and therapeutics. Comparison with the work on EBOV, SUDV and MARV gives a useful perspective on what is possible. Evidence mapping pro- vides a novel approach to support the research community, accelerat- ing research to resolve the current BDBV outbreak and providing a key tool to support research on future health threats. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for rapid research response during a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, specifically the Bundibugyo virus outbreak, by providing an organized resource to guide immunological and microbiological research.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved evidence mapping of filovirus research, focusing on human-pathogenic orthoebolaviruses and related entities such as Bundibugyo virus, Sudan virus, and Taï Forest virus. The research was conducted in the context of a global health emergency, with the goal of enabling researchers to quickly identify relevant literature.
analysis.methods: The evidence mapping process systematically identified and categorized publications according to population, intervention, and outcomes. Two independent reviewers performed the screening and mapping to ensure consistency and unbiased representation of the literature.
analysis.main_results: The evidence map was created to provide a comprehensive overview of the literature on filoviruses, including the Bundibugyo virus, and was designed to be a dynamic resource that can be updated regularly to maintain its relevance.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as a novel approach to accelerate research responses during health emergencies, emphasizing the utility of evidence mapping in providing an organized and accessible resource for the research community.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the rapid development of vaccines, treatments, and diagnostics for emerging infectious diseases like the Bundibugyo virus, supporting more efficient and targeted research efforts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on existing literature and the potential for bias in the selection and categorization of publications. However, the evidence mapping process is designed to be comprehensive and unbiased, providing a moderate level of confidence in its utility for guiding future research.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents an evidence mapping approach to accelerate research responses during the Bundibugyo virus emergency. The research community requires rapid access to information to guide effective action, and evidence mapping provides a structured resource to identify priorities, gaps, and opportunities for action. The evidence map categorizes publications based on population, intervention, and outcomes, offering a dynamic and unbiased overview of the literature. This resource can inform the development of vaccines, treatments, and diagnostics for emerging infectious diseases, including the Bundibugyo virus. The study's limitations include reliance on existing literature and potential bias in the mapping process, but the systematic approach ensures a moderate level of confidence in its findings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过提供有组织的资源来指导免疫学和微生物学研究,以满足国际关注的突发公共卫生事件(特别是本迪布焦病毒 暴发)期间快速研究响应的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及丝状病毒研究的证据图谱,重点关注人类致病性正埃博拉病毒和相关实体,如本迪布焦病毒、苏丹病毒和塔伊森林病毒。该研究是在全球卫生紧急情况的背景下进行的,目的是使研究人员能够快速识别相关文献。
elements_zh.methods: 证据映射过程根据人口、干预措施和结果系统地识别和分类出版物。两名独立评审员进行了筛选和绘图,以确保文献的一致性和公正性。
elements_zh.main_results: 创建证据图是为了提供有关丝状病毒(包括本迪布焦病毒)的文献的全面概述,并被设计为可以定期更新以保持其相关性的动态资源。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为一种在突发卫生事件期间加速研究响应的新方法,强调了证据映射在为研究界提供有组织且可访问的资源方面的效用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为 疫苗、治疗 和本迪布焦病毒等新发传染病的诊断方法的快速发展提供信息,支持更高效、更有针对性的研究工作。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对现有文献的依赖以及出版物的选择和分类方面可能存在偏见而受到限制。然而,证据映射过程的设计是全面且公正的,为其指导未来研究的效用提供了一定程度的信心。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及丝状病毒研究的证据图谱,重点关注人类致病性正埃博拉病毒和相关实体,如本迪布焦病毒、苏丹病毒和塔伊森林病毒。该研究是在全球卫生紧急情况的背景下进行的,目的是使研究人员能够快速识别相关文献。
analysis_zh.methods: 证据映射过程根据人口、干预措施和结果系统地识别和分类出版物。两名独立评审员进行了筛选和绘图,以确保文献的一致性和公正性。

papers.title: TRUST, RUMOURS, AND RESPONSE LEGITIMACY IN THE 2026 BUNDIBUGYO VIRUS DISEASE OUTBREAK IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO A desk-based qualitative synthesis
papers.abstract: The 2026 outbreak of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo developed into a major public-health emergency in a setting marked by armed insecurity, population mobility, weak routine health services and previous experience of externally led Ebola responses. Alongside the epidemiological emergency, response agencies documented doubts about whether the outbreak was real, suspicions that it was being used for financial or political purposes, concerns about treatment and isolation, and confrontations around the handling of the dead. These narratives raise a central operational question: under what conditions do communities consider an epidemic response credible, fair and morally legitimate?We conducted a desk-based qualitative synthesis of publicly available materials relating to the outbreak, identified up to 5 August 2026. The outbreak-specific corpus included World Health Organization and Africa Infodemic Response Alliance social-listening reports, disease outbreak notices and situation reports, International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies community-feedback reporting, the Social Science in Humanitarian Action Platform rapid synthesis, operational statements and selected media accounts. These materials were triangulated with peer-reviewed research on institutional trust, community feedback and the atmosphere of mistrust during the 2018–2020 Ebola epidemic in eastern DRC. The available evidence identified several connected narrative clusters: claims that Ebola was invented or exaggerated; the recurrent idea that “Ebola is a business”; allegations of political manipulation or external intervention; suspicion of medicines, disinfectants, experimental products and treatment centres; uncertainty about how patients could recover without a licensed treatment; and rumours concerning burials, bodies and empty coffins. These narratives were not expressions of biomedical ignorance alone. They interpreted the outbreak through prior experiences of corruption, unequal resource distribution, inadequate routine services, coercive authority and limited transparency. Operational reports linked these concerns to delayed care-seeking, resistance to referral and isolation, incomplete contact tracing, burial tensions and hostility towards responders. Local volunteers, survivors and trusted community intermediaries appeared capable of improving credibility, although the available evidence did not support a representative ranking of trusted institutions.Trust should be treated as part of outbreak-control infrastructure rather than as an attitudinal outcome of communication. Response legitimacy is produced through the conduct of the response: transparent explanation of case figures and procedures, fair and visible use of resources, respectful treatment of patients and families, locally credible messengers, practical opportunities for community participation, and demonstrable adaptation to feedback.

analysis.summary_en: This desk-based qualitative synthesis examined why communities doubted the legitimacy of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak response in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. papers.title_zh: 刚果民主共和国 2026 年本迪布焦病毒病 暴发 的信任、谣言和应对合法性 基于案头的定性综合
papers.source_body_en: The 2026 outbreak of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo developed into a major public-health emergency in a setting marked by armed insecurity, population mobility, weak routine health services and previous experience of externally led Ebola responses. Alongside the epidemiological emergency, response agencies documented doubts about whether the outbreak was real, suspicions that it was being used for financial or political purposes, concerns about treatment and isolation, and confrontations around the handling of the dead. These narratives raise a central operational question: under what conditions do communities consider an epidemic response credible, fair and morally legitimate?We conducted a desk-based qualitative synthesis of publicly available materials relating to the outbreak, identified up to 5 August 2026. The outbreak-specific corpus included World Health Organization and Africa Infodemic Response Alliance social-listening reports, disease outbreak notices and situation reports, International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies community-feedback reporting, the Social Science in Humanitarian Action Platform rapid synthesis, operational statements and selected media accounts. These materials were triangulated with peer-reviewed research on institutional trust, community feedback and the atmosphere of mistrust during the 2018–2020 Ebola epidemic in eastern DRC. The available evidence identified several connected narrative clusters: claims that Ebola was invented or exaggerated; the recurrent idea that “Ebola is a business”; allegations of political manipulation or external intervention; suspicion of medicines, disinfectants, experimental products and treatment centres; uncertainty about how patients could recover without a licensed treatment; and rumours concerning burials, bodies and empty coffins. These narratives were not expressions of biomedical ignorance alone. They interpreted the outbreak through prior experiences of corruption, unequal resource distribution, inadequate routine services, coercive authority and limited transparency. Operational reports linked these concerns to delayed care-seeking, resistance to referral and isolation, incomplete contact tracing, burial tensions and hostility towards responders. Local volunteers, survivors and trusted community intermediaries appeared capable of improving credibility, although the available evidence did not support a representative ranking of trusted institutions.Trust should be treated as part of outbreak-control infrastructure rather than as an attitudinal outcome of communication. Response legitimacy is produced through the conduct of the response: transparent explanation of case figures and procedures, fair and visible use of resources, respectful treatment of patients and families, locally credible messengers, practical opportunities for community participation, and demonstrable adaptation to feedback.
papers.abstract_zh: 2026 年 暴发 刚果民主共和国由本迪布焦病毒引起的埃博拉疫情发展成为重大公共卫生紧急事件,其特点是武装不安全、人口流动、常规卫生服务薄弱以及以往外部主导的埃博拉应对经验。除了流行病学紧急情况外,响应机构还记录了对 暴发 是否真实的怀疑、怀疑它被用于金融或政治目的、对 暴发 和隔离的担忧,以及围绕处理死者的对抗。这些叙述提出了一个核心操作问题:在什么条件下,社区认为流行病应对措施是可信的、公平的和道德上合法的?我们对截至 2026 年 8 月 5 日确定的与 暴发 相关的公开材料进行了案头定性综合。暴发 特定语料库包括世界卫生组织和非洲信息流行病应对联盟的社交聆听报告、疾病 暴发 通知和情况报告、红十字国际联合会和红新月会社区反馈报告、人道主义行动社会科学平台快速综合、业务声明和选定的媒体报道。这些材料与同行评审的研究进行了三角测量,这些研究涉及 2018-2020 年刚果民主共和国东部埃博拉疫情期间的机构信任、社区反馈和不信任气氛。现有证据确定了几个相互关联的叙述集群:声称埃博拉病毒是发明或夸大的;声称埃博拉病毒是虚构的或夸大的;“埃博拉病毒是一门生意”这一反复出现的想法;政治操纵或外部干预的指控;怀疑药品、消毒剂、实验产品和 治疗 中心;如果没有 治疗 许可,患者如何康复存在不确定性;以及有关埋葬、尸体和空棺材的谣言。这些叙述不仅仅是生物医学无知的表现。他们通过以往的腐败、资源分配不平等、日常服务不足、强制权威和有限透明度的经验来解释《暴发》。行动报告将这些担忧与延迟寻求护理、拒绝转诊和隔离、不完整的接触者追踪、埋葬紧张以及对救护人员的敌意联系起来。尽管现有证据不支持可信机构的代表性排名,但当地志愿者、幸存者和值得信赖的社区中介似乎能够提高可信度。信任应被视为 暴发 控制基础设施的一部分,而不是沟通的态度结果。响应的合法性是通过响应的实施来产生的:对病例数字和程序的透明解释、公平和可见的资源使用、患者和家属的尊重治疗、当地可信的信息传递者、社区参与的实际机会以及对反馈的明显适应。

papers.title: Rapid and portable reverse-transcription quantitative PCR assays for Bundibugyo ebolavirus detection
papers.abstract: The 2026 Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) outbreak underscores the need for rapidly deployable molecular diagnostics. We developed and analytically validated reverse-transcription quantitative PCR assays detecting BDBV, Zaire ebolavirus, and Sudan ebolavirus. The platform includes a BDBV singleplex assay, a duplex assay with a human internal control, a four-target multiplex assay for ebolavirus differentiation, and a probe-free SYBR Green assay. We adapted the assays to a portable qPCR instrument, reducing runtime from 65 to 35 minutes, and validated lyophilized reagents to reduce cold-chain requirements. All TaqMan formats achieved a 95% limit of detection of 5 copies per reaction across instruments and reagent types; the SYBR Green assay achieved 50 copies per reaction. The assays detected viral RNA in contrived clinical samples without cross-reactivity among ebolavirus species tested. We shared the protocols in real time through Ampliphi (https://www.ampliphi.bio), a new open-access platform for rapidly disseminating diagnostic assays, and through protocol.io.

papers.title: BURIAL, MOURNING, AND THE SOCIAL ORGANIZATION OF CARE IN THE 2026 BUNDIBUGYO VIRUS DISEASE OUTBREAK IN THE DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF THE CONGO A desk-based qualitative synthesis
papers.abstract: BackgroundBurial is among the most epidemiologically consequential and socially sensitive components of Ebola response. During the 2026 outbreak of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, public-health agencies documented confrontations with burial teams, rumours about empty or opened coffins, questions about why families could not see or touch the dead, and delays in safe and dignified burial operations. These events were often described as community resistance. This paper instead examines burial as a moral, relational and practical process through which families care for the dead, organise grief, negotiate authority and restore social order.MethodsWe conducted a desk-based qualitative synthesis of outbreak-specific materials available up to 5 August 2026, including World Health Organization and Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention reports, infodemic monitoring, key-message guidance, Red Cross reporting, social-science syntheses and a 2026 contextual note on funeral practices in Ituri. These were triangulated with peer-reviewed studies of safe and dignified burial, burial workers, gendered caregiving and community feedback from earlier Ebola outbreaks. Sources were coded for the social stages of burial, family authority, ritual obligations, gendered labour, conflict points, operational delays, adaptations and behavioural consequences.FindingsBurial was not a single technical act but a sequence extending from end-of-life care and body preparation to viewing, transport, prayer, interment and continued mourning. The legitimacy of safe burial depended on whether families could identify the body, understand each procedure, retain recognised roles and participate in decisions about clothing, burial place, religious observance and commemoration. Conflict concentrated around rapid removal without explanation, limited visual access, uncertainty about testing and decontamination, delays in burial-team arrival, the presence of unfamiliar responders and procedures perceived as disrespectful. Women and relatives of the same sex as the deceased appeared especially exposed through caregiving and body preparation, although the available outbreak data could not quantify gender-specific risk. Locally recruited teams, family liaison, safe visual confirmation, ritual substitution, timely response and grief-sensitive communication were the most consistently supported adaptations.InterpretationDignity and infection control are not competing objectives. A burial becomes epidemiologically effective when it is socially recognisable as a burial and when families have defensible reasons to trust what is happening to the body. Safe and dignified burial should therefore be managed as a negotiated care pathway, with timeliness, family participation, body-identification assurance, gender-sensitive risk assessment and family satisfaction treated as operational performance indicators.

papers.source_body_en: BackgroundBurial is among the most epidemiologically consequential and socially sensitive components of Ebola response. During the 2026 outbreak of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, public-health agencies documented confrontations with burial teams, rumours about empty or opened coffins, questions about why families could not see or touch the dead, and delays in safe and dignified burial operations. These events were often described as community resistance. This paper instead examines burial as a moral, relational and practical process through which families care for the dead, organise grief, negotiate authority and restore social order.MethodsWe conducted a desk-based qualitative synthesis of outbreak-specific materials available up to 5 August 2026, including World Health Organization and Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention reports, infodemic monitoring, key-message guidance, Red Cross reporting, social-science syntheses and a 2026 contextual note on funeral practices in Ituri. These were triangulated with peer-reviewed studies of safe and dignified burial, burial workers, gendered caregiving and community feedback from earlier Ebola outbreaks. Sources were coded for the social stages of burial, family authority, ritual obligations, gendered labour, conflict points, operational delays, adaptations and behavioural consequences.FindingsBurial was not a single technical act but a sequence extending from end-of-life care and body preparation to viewing, transport, prayer, interment and continued mourning. The legitimacy of safe burial depended on whether families could identify the body, understand each procedure, retain recognised roles and participate in decisions about clothing, burial place, religious observance and commemoration. Conflict concentrated around rapid removal without explanation, limited visual access, uncertainty about testing and decontamination, delays in burial-team arrival, the presence of unfamiliar responders and procedures perceived as disrespectful. Women and relatives of the same sex as the deceased appeared especially exposed through caregiving and body preparation, although the available outbreak data could not quantify gender-specific risk. Locally recruited teams, family liaison, safe visual confirmation, ritual substitution, timely response and grief-sensitive communication were the most consistently supported adaptations.InterpretationDignity and infection control are not competing objectives. A burial becomes epidemiologically effective when it is socially recognisable as a burial and when families have defensible reasons to trust what is happening to the body. Safe and dignified burial should therefore be managed as a negotiated care pathway, with timeliness, family participation, body-identification assurance, gender-sensitive risk assessment and family satisfaction treated as operational performance indicators.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景埋葬是埃博拉应对措施中最具流行病学意义和社会敏感性的组成部分之一。2026 年刚果民主共和国本迪布焦病毒引起的埃博拉疫情期间,公共卫生机构记录了与埋葬团队的对抗、关于空棺材或打开棺材的谣言、关于为什么家人无法看到或触摸死者的问题,以及安全和有尊严的埋葬作业的延误。这些事件通常被描述为社区抵抗。相反,本文将埋葬视为一种道德、关系和实际的过程,通过这个过程,家庭照顾死者、组织悲伤、协商权威和恢复社会秩序。方法我们对截至 2026 年 8 月 5 日可用的 暴发 特定材料进行了案头定性综合,包括世界卫生组织和非洲疾病控制和预防中心的报告、信息流行病监测、关键信息指导、红十字会报告、社会科学综合和 2026 年有关丧葬问题的背景说明伊图里的葬礼习俗。这些研究与有关安全和有尊严的埋葬、埋葬工作人员、性别护理以及早期埃博拉 暴发 社区反馈的同行评审研究进行了三角测量。对埋葬的社会阶段、家庭权威、仪式义务、性别劳动、冲突点、操作延迟、适应和行为后果进行了编码。调查结果埋葬不是单一的技术行为,而是从临终关怀和身体准备到观看、运输、祈祷、埋葬和持续哀悼的一系列过程。安全埋葬的合法性取决于家人是否能够识别尸体、了解每个程序、保留公认的角色并参与有关服装、埋葬地点、宗教仪式和纪念活动的决策。冲突集中在没有解释的情况下快速清除、视线有限、测试和净化的不确定性、埋葬团队抵达的延误、不熟悉的响应人员的存在以及被认为不尊重的程序。尽管现有的 暴发 数据无法量化特定性别的风险,但女性和与死者同性别的亲属似乎尤其容易因护理和身体准备而受到暴露。当地招募的团队、家庭联络、安全视觉确认、仪式替代、及时反应和悲伤敏感的沟通是最一致支持的适应措施。解释尊严和感染控制不是相互竞争的目标。当埋葬被社会认可为埋葬,并且家人有充分的理由相信尸体发生的情况时,埋葬在流行病学上就变得有效。因此,安全和有尊严的埋葬应作为协商的护理途径进行管理,并将及时性、家庭参与、尸体身份确认、性别敏感风险评估和家庭满意度视为运营绩效指标。

papers.full_text: The World Health Organization (WHO) has recommended prioritising the Ervebo vaccine for testing in a clinical trial in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The vaccine was originally developed to protect against Zaire ebolavirus, the species responsible for the devastating west African epidemic just over a decade ago. It was not designed for the Bundibugyo species responsible for the current outbreak – which raises the question of why scientists are considering it at all. The current Ebola outbreak was declared a public health emergency of international concern in May 2026. By August 9, there had been 4,402 confirmed cases and 2,013 deaths. All but 21 of these cases were reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with 20 cases in Uganda and one in France. These figures make the current outbreak the second-largest Ebola epidemic on record, surpassed only by the west African epidemic of 2014–16, where 11,000 people died. At present, there are around 75–100 new cases being reported each day. The UN has described it as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak ever recorded. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the director general of the WHO, said the current outbreak is on track to become the world’s largest. Unfortunately, there is still no clear evidence that the outbreak is coming under control, and the number of infections may still be rising rapidly. Ebola outbreaks are usually brought under control through a combination of vaccination and public health measures. During an outbreak, vaccines can be particularly effective, especially when used quickly. Health authorities may carry out large-scale vaccination campaigns. They can also use a strategy known as “ring vaccination”. This involves offering the vaccine to people who have been in close contact with someone who has been infected. The aim is to create a protective ring around each case and stop the virus from spreading further. Public health measures are also crucial. These include finding cases early, tracing contacts and moving infected people to specialist treatment centres where they can be cared for safely and isolated from others until they recover. Caring for someone who is seriously ill with Ebola carries a particularly high risk of infection. Public education is also important, including advice on caring for patients safely and reducing the risk of transmission during funerals. No licensed vaccine The challenge is that, unlike the Zaire species of Ebola, there is currently no licensed vaccine for Bundibugyo virus disease. There are also no licensed vaccines for some other Ebola species, including Sudan virus disease and Taï Forest virus disease. As a result, vaccination has not yet played a role in controlling the outbreak. Several Bundibugyo vaccines are under development. Two have already entered phase 1 clinical trials. One has been developed by Oxford University and the Serum Institute of India, while another is being developed by Moderna. Read more: Two scientists on their race to make a new Ebola vaccine A phase 1 clinical trial is the first stage of testing a new vaccine in people. These studies are mainly designed to assess safety and identify any side-effects. It is not yet clear how long it will take before these vaccines could become widely available if they prove successful. Neither are being tested in Africa. Without a vaccine, efforts to control the outbreak depend entirely on public health measures. But putting these measures into practice can be difficult, especially during a fast-moving outbreak. Fear and uncertainty are common during outbreaks of dangerous diseases. Misinformation and rumours can spread quickly. During the west African Ebola epidemic, reports suggested that some families hid sick relatives because they feared they would be taken away by health authorities. In some settings, there have also been reports of mistrust towards official responses to outbreaks and concerns about the motives of outside organisations involved in disease control efforts. The current situation in the DRC is made even more difficult by the ongoing armed conflict in some of the affected areas. Conflict can make it much harder for health workers to reach communities, track cases and implement control measures. There have already been several attacks on Ebola treatment centres in the country this year. In one incident, a treatment centre was set on fire after a dispute over the handling of the body of an infected person. Another worrying sign is that many newly diagnosed patients had not previously been identified as contacts of earlier cases. This suggests that the virus may be spreading unnoticed in some communities. Against this backdrop, the WHO advisory group has recommended testing the Ervebo vaccine. papers.title: Deadbolt Drug Discovery: Locking the Door to Class 1 Viral Entry by Small Molecules.
papers.abstract: The continued emergence of viral pathogens underscores the need for novel antiviral therapeutics with improved efficacy. Small-molecule inhibitors of viral entry are attractive antiviral agents because they block the virus at its earliest step, preventing the virus from entering host cells and causing downstream damage. Some of the viruses of greatest concern for human health, such as human immunodeficiency virus, respiratory syncytial virus, influenza virus, Ebola virus, severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, and Lassa virus, encode Class 1 fusion proteins which mediate membrane fusion and viral entry. In this review, we highlight recent advances in the discovery and development of small-molecule entry inhibitors reported over the past five years that target viruses encoding Class 1 fusion proteins.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the development of small-molecule inhibitors targeting Class 1 viral entry proteins, specifically in the context of Ebola viruses and related pathogens. The central question is whether these inhibitors can effectively block viral entry and serve as potential antiviral therapeutics for diseases caused by these viruses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of recent advances in small-molecule entry inhibitors targeting viruses with Class 1 fusion proteins. It includes studies from the past five years and highlights the mechanisms of action and efficacy of these inhibitors against specific viral targets.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that small-molecule inhibitors targeting Class 1 fusion proteins have shown promise in preventing viral entry, which is a critical early step in infection. These inhibitors are considered attractive candidates for antiviral therapy due to their ability to block the virus before it causes significant damage to host cells.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while there is agreement on the potential of these inhibitors, the evidence is still limited in terms of long-term efficacy and safety. Additionally, the review highlights the need for more research on the effectiveness of these inhibitors against a broader range of related viruses.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that further research is needed to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of small-molecule entry inhibitors against Ebola viruses and related pathogens. It also emphasizes the importance of expanding studies to include more diverse populations and geographic regions.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the development of small-molecule inhibitors targeting Class 1 viral entry proteins, with a focus on Ebola viruses and related pathogens. It highlights recent advances in the field and underscores the potential of these inhibitors as antiviral agents. The review identifies the need for more research on their long-term efficacy and safety, as well as their application across diverse populations and regions. While the evidence supports the effectiveness of these inhibitors in blocking viral entry, there are still gaps in understanding their broader implications for antiviral therapy.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述的重点是针对 1 类病毒进入蛋白的小分子抑制剂的开发,特别是在 埃博拉病毒 和相关病原体的背景下。核心问题是这些抑制剂是否可以有效阻止病毒进入并作为治疗这些病毒引起的疾病的潜在 抗病毒药物 疗法。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对带有 1 类融合蛋白的针对病毒的小分子进入抑制剂的最新进展的叙述性综合。它包括过去五年的研究,并强调了这些抑制剂针对特定病毒靶标的作用机制和功效。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,针对 1 类融合蛋白的小分子抑制剂在防止病毒进入方面显示出前景,这是感染的关键早期步骤。这些抑制剂被认为是 抗病毒药物 治疗的有吸引力的候选者,因为它们能够在病毒对 宿主 细胞造成重大损害之前阻断病毒。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 审查指出,虽然人们对这些抑制剂的潜力达成了一致,但在长期疗效和安全性方面的证据仍然有限。此外,该评论强调需要对这些抑制剂针对更广泛的相关病毒的有效性进行更多研究。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述表明,需要进一步研究来评估小分子进入抑制剂针对 埃博拉病毒 和相关病原体的长期安全性和有效性。它还强调了扩大研究范围以涵盖更多样化的人群和地理区域的重要性。

papers.title: High-Resolution Mapping of Environmental Suitability for Reported Ebola Spillover Events in Uganda to Inform Surveillance and Preparedness.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Uganda experiences recurrent Ebola disease (EBOD) outbreaks, yet national suitability maps often pool virus species or are too coarse for district-level planning. We aimed to generate species-resolved, 1 km relative environmental suitability surfaces for reported Ebola spillover events in Uganda; quantify the contribution of environmental, anthropogenic, and reservoir-related predictors to modeled suitability; and translate continuous outputs into operational prioritization tiers for district surveillance and preparedness. METHODS: We compiled 71 laboratory-confirmed reported Ebola event localities in Uganda from 2000 to 2023, defined as the most likely documented locality of initial human infection where available, and paired them with 11 minimally collinear predictors. Pooled and virus-specific MaxEnt models were tuned in ENMeval by comparing feature-class sets across β = 0.5 to 3.0, ranked by AICc, and screened for acceptable omission at the 10% training-presence threshold. Performance was estimated using fourfold spatial block cross-validation. Pooled cloglog suitability values were thresholded at the 10% training-presence value and stratified into four operational prioritization tiers. RESULTS: Tuning selected LQHP with β = 1.5 for the pooled model. Under spatial block cross-validation, pooled performance was Test AUC = 0.845 (0.825 to 0.862) and Test Boyce = 0.58 (0.52 to 0.63), with Test OR10 = 0.101 (0.092 to 0.109). The operational threshold was cloglog = 0.084, classifying 25.4% of Uganda as suitable within the modeling framework. Tier 1, defined as the highest-suitability decile among suitable pixels (cloglog ≥ 0.65), covered 5.8% of land area yet contained approximately 12.6 million residents (29%). High-suitability areas were clustered in the Albertine Rift escarpment belt, the Kampala, Wakiso, Mukono peri-urban cluster extending along major corridors, and a northern Lake Kyoga shoreline crescent. Species-specific outputs were interpreted as exploratory secondary analyses. SUDV broadly reproduced the pooled modeled suitability geography, EBOV showed elevated suitability along the western border corridor, and BDBV suitability was concentrated around the Albertine escarpment. Checkerboard2 sensitivity produced a small AUC increase (ΔAUC = +0.006) and high tier agreement. CONCLUSIONS: Relative environmental suitability for reported Ebola spillover localities in Uganda is concentrated in compact high-priority belts where elevated modeled suitability overlaps with large resident populations. Tier 1 and Tier 2 areas provide a focused basis for strengthening event-based surveillance, early detection, laboratory referral, infection prevention and control readiness, rapid response capacity, One Health field investigation, and community engagement.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to generate high-resolution environmental suitability maps for reported Ebola spillover events in Uganda, focusing on species-specific models to guide surveillance and preparedness. The researchers compiled 71 laboratory-confirmed event localities from 2000 to 2023 and paired them with 11 minimally collinear predictors. They used MaxEnt models tuned via ENMeval and validated performance using fourfold spatial block cross-validation. The results showed that the pooled model selected LQHP with β = 1.5, achieving a Test AUC of 0.845 and Test Boyce of 0.58. The operational threshold classified 25.4% of Uganda as suitable, with Tier 1 areas covering 5.8% of the land and containing 29% of the population. High-suitability areas were concentrated in specific geographic regions, and species-specific outputs were interpreted as exploratory. The findings suggest that targeted surveillance and preparedness efforts should focus on these high-priority belts to enhance outbreak response capabilities.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 乌干达埃博拉疫情 (EBOD) 暴发 反复出现,但国家适宜性地图经常汇集病毒种类,或者对于地区级规划来说过于粗略。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们的目标是为乌干达报告的埃博拉 跨物种溢出 事件生成物种解析的 1 公里相对环境适宜性表面;量化环境、人为和 储存宿主 相关预测因素对建模适宜性的贡献;并将持续产出转化为地区 监测 和准备工作的操作优先级。
elements_zh.methods: 我们编制了 2000 年至 2023 年乌干达 71 个经实验室确认报告的埃博拉事件地点,定义为最有可能记录的人类初始感染地点,并将它们与 11 个最小共线预测因子配对。
elements_zh.main_results: 为合并模型调整选定的 LQHP,β = 1.5。在空间块交叉验证下,汇总性能为测试 AUC = 0.845(0.825 至 0.862)和测试 Boyce = 0.58(0.52 至 0.63),测试 OR10 = 0.101(0.092 至 0.109)。操作阈值为 cloglog = 0.084,将乌干达的 25.4% 分类为适合建模框架。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 乌干达报告的埃博拉病毒 跨物种溢出 地区的相对环境适宜性集中在紧凑的高优先级地带,这些地带的模型适宜性与大量居民人口重叠。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 第 1 级和第 2 级领域为加强基于事件的 监测、早期检测、实验室转诊、感染预防和控制准备、快速反应能力、One Health 现场调查和社区参与提供了重点基础。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 使用四重空间块交叉验证来估计性能。

papers.title_zh: 乌干达报告的埃博拉 跨物种溢出 事件的环境适宜性高分辨率绘图,为 监测 和准备工作提供信息。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Uganda experiences recurrent Ebola disease (EBOD) outbreaks, yet national suitability maps often pool virus species or are too coarse for district-level planning. We aimed to generate species-resolved, 1 km relative environmental suitability surfaces for reported Ebola spillover events in Uganda; quantify the contribution of environmental, anthropogenic, and reservoir-related predictors to modeled suitability; and translate continuous outputs into operational prioritization tiers for district surveillance and preparedness. METHODS: We compiled 71 laboratory-confirmed reported Ebola event localities in Uganda from 2000 to 2023, defined as the most likely documented locality of initial human infection where available, and paired them with 11 minimally collinear predictors. Pooled and virus-specific MaxEnt models were tuned in ENMeval by comparing feature-class sets across β = 0.5 to 3.0, ranked by AICc, and screened for acceptable omission at the 10% training-presence threshold. Performance was estimated using fourfold spatial block cross-validation. Pooled cloglog suitability values were thresholded at the 10% training-presence value and stratified into four operational prioritization tiers. RESULTS: Tuning selected LQHP with β = 1.5 for the pooled model. Under spatial block cross-validation, pooled performance was Test AUC = 0.845 (0.825 to 0.862) and Test Boyce = 0.58 (0.52 to 0.63), with Test OR10 = 0.101 (0.092 to 0.109). The operational threshold was cloglog = 0.084, classifying 25.4% of Uganda as suitable within the modeling framework. Tier 1, defined as the highest-suitability decile among suitable pixels (cloglog ≥ 0.65), covered 5.8% of land area yet contained approximately 12.6 million residents (29%). High-suitability areas were clustered in the Albertine Rift escarpment belt, the Kampala, Wakiso, Mukono peri-urban cluster extending along major corridors, and a northern Lake Kyoga shoreline crescent. Species-specific outputs were interpreted as exploratory secondary analyses. SUDV broadly reproduced the pooled modeled suitability geography, EBOV showed elevated suitability along the western border corridor, and BDBV suitability was concentrated around the Albertine escarpment. Checkerboard2 sensitivity produced a small AUC increase (ΔAUC = +0.006) and high tier agreement. CONCLUSIONS: Relative environmental suitability for reported Ebola spillover localities in Uganda is concentrated in compact high-priority belts where elevated modeled suitability overlaps with large resident populations. Tier 1 and Tier 2 areas provide a focused basis for strengthening event-based surveillance, early detection, laboratory referral, infection prevention and control readiness, rapid response capacity, One Health field investigation, and community engagement.

papers.title: Dynamics, Optimal Control, and Spillover Risk of the 2026 Bundibugyo Ebola Outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
papers.abstract: In 2026, a Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) outbreak emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with 4,566 confirmed cases and 2,128 deaths reported as of 11 August, potentially becoming the largest Ebola outbreak on record globally. We developed a susceptible-exposed-infectious-deceased-recovered (SEIDR) model incorporating incorporating three categories of interventions, public self-protection, safe burial, and treatment and convalescence, to assess early transmission dynamics, the current epidemic trajectory, and cross-border spillover risk, and to inform the formulation of control strategies. Based on cumulative confirmed case data up to 31 July, sensitivity analyses across multiple candidate start dates identified 28 March as the optimal start date of sustained transmission, with 31 March to 3 April as the most likely onset window. As of 31 July, the basic reproduction number (R0) was 1.83 (95% CI: 1.81-1.84). When 58.12% of the susceptible population adopted protective behaviours, the transmission chain could be effectively interrupted. By integrating the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) with Pontryagin's minimum principle (PMP), we derived a time-varying optimal control strategy, with adjustments every two weeks, that could shorten the epidemic duration by approximately 7 months. Using International Migrant Stock data and Facebook IP-based mobility data with the Prophet forecasting model, we assessed spillover risk. Four countries were identified as very high risk at the end of July. Compared with the status quo scenario, the optimised control strategy could substantially reduce global importation risk. Enhanced entry screening and preparedness are warranted in neighbouring countries of the DRC in Africa, France in Europe, and Canada in North America.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the dynamics of the 2026 Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and assess its spillover risk to inform control strategies. The outbreak, with 4,566 confirmed cases and 2,128 deaths as of 11 August 2026, potentially became the largest Ebola outbreak on record.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A susceptible-exposed-infectious-deceased-recovered (SEIDR) model was developed to evaluate early transmission dynamics, the current epidemic trajectory, and cross-border spillover risk. The model incorporated three categories of interventions: public self-protection, safe burial, and treatment and convalescence.
analysis.methods: The study used International Migrant Stock data and Facebook IP-based mobility data with the Prophet forecasting model to assess spillover risk. Sensitivity analyses across multiple candidate start dates identified 28 March as the optimal start date of sustained transmission.
analysis.main_results: As of 31 July 2026, the basic reproduction number (R0) was 1.83 (95% CI: 1.81-1.84). When 58.12% of the susceptible population adopted protective behaviours, the transmission chain could be effectively interrupted.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that a significant proportion of the population adopting protective measures could interrupt the transmission chain. The study introduced an integrated model combining non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) with Pontryagin's minimum principle (PMP) to derive a time-varying optimal control strategy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted control strategies to mitigate the spread of the Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) outbreak in the DRC and reduce global importation risk. Enhanced entry screening and preparedness are warranted in neighboring countries.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relied on cumulative confirmed case data up to 31 July 2026, which may limit the accuracy of transmission dynamics modeling. The evidence strength is moderate due to the use of abstract-only data and the assumptions inherent in the forecasting model.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the 2026 Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), identifying it as potentially the largest Ebola outbreak on record with 4,566 confirmed cases and 2,128 deaths. Using a susceptible-exposed-infectious-deceased-recovered (SEIDR) model, the researchers assessed transmission dynamics and spillover risk, incorporating interventions such as public self-protection, safe burial, and treatment. The basic reproduction number (R0) was estimated at 1.83 (95% CI: 1.81-1.84), and the model suggested that 58.12% of the susceptible population adopting protective behaviors could interrupt transmission. An optimized control strategy using NSGA-II and Pontryagin's minimum principle was proposed to reduce the epidemic duration by approximately 7 months. The study highlights the importance of enhanced entry screening and preparedness in neighboring countries to mitigate global importation risk. However, the reliance on abstract-only data and assumptions in the forecasting model limits the confidence in the findings, resulting in a moderate evidence strength assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在了解 2026 年本迪布焦埃博拉病毒 (BDBV) 暴发 在刚果民主共和国 (DRC) 的动态,并评估其 跨物种溢出 风险,为控制策略提供信息。截至 2026 年 8 月 11 日,暴发 已有 4,566 例确诊病例和 2,128 人死亡,有可能成为有记录以来最大的埃博拉 暴发。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 开发了易感者-暴露-感染者-死亡者-康复(SEIDR)模型来评估早期传播动态、当前的流行轨迹和跨境传播风险。该模型纳入了三类干预措施:公众自我保护、安全埋葬、治疗 和康复。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用国际移民存量数据和 Facebook 基于 IP 的流动性数据以及 Prophet 预测模型来评估 跨物种溢出 风险。对多个候选开始日期的敏感性分析确定 3 月 28 日是持续 传播 的最佳开始日期。
elements_zh.main_results: 截至2026年7月31日,基本再生数(R0)为1.83(95% CI:1.81-1.84)。当58.12%的易感人群采取保护行为时,传播链可以被有效中断。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为表明很大一部分人群采取的保护措施可能会中断 传播 链。该研究引入了一种将非支配排序遗传算法 II (NSGA-II) 与庞特里亚金最小原理 (PMP) 相结合的集成模型,以导出时变最优控制策略。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为制定有针对性的控制策略提供信息,以减轻本迪布焦埃博拉病毒(BDBV)暴发在刚果民主共和国的传播,并降低全球输入风险。邻国有必要加强入境筛查和准备工作。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖截至2026年7月31日的累积确诊病例数据,这可能会限制传播动力学模型的准确性。由于仅使用抽象数据和预测模型固有的假设,证据强度中等。

papers.title: A qualitative participatory study on adolescent mental health and well-being in Sierra Leone
papers.abstract: Adolescents in Sierra Leone have endured successive crises including civil conflict, the 2014 to 2016 Ebola virus disease outbreak, and the COVID-19 pandemic, each compounding pre-existing vulnerabilities in mental health, education, and family stability. Despite growing global recognition of adolescent mental health as a public health priority, qualitative evidence documenting how young Sierra Leoneans experience distress, coping, and recovery remains limited. This study examined how adolescents in Sierra Leone experience mental health, well-being, coping, schooling, and post-crisis recovery. A qualitative participatory study was conducted across three districts in Sierra Leone between February and July 2024. Purposive sampling recruited 112 participants, including adolescents aged 13 to 19 years, caregivers, teachers, youth leaders, community health workers, counsellors, and child protection actors. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, focus group discussions, emotion mapping, personal timelines, and guided storytelling. Reflexive thematic analysis was applied. We identified four themes: (1) landscapes of distress, encompassing grief, fear, poverty-related shame, and school disruption; (2) gendered and intersecting vulnerabilities, including early marriage, sexual violence, and differential educational access; (3) coping, resilience, and meaning-making through faith, peer solidarity, creative expression, and aspiration; and (4) navigating support, revealing trust barriers, stigma, and the centrality of informal networks. Adolescent mental health in Sierra Leone is shaped by layered, intersecting crises that exceed individual-level coping. School-based psychosocial support, community-level stigma reduction, and gender-responsive services are urgently needed.
papers.journal: Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and Mental Health

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 这项研究是必要的,因为塞拉利昂的青少年面临着分层危机——内战、2014-2016 埃博拉病毒病 暴发 和 COVID-19——这些危机加剧了心理健康、教育和家庭稳定方面本来就存在的脆弱性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024 年 2 月至 7 月期间,在塞拉利昂的三个地区进行了一项定性参与性研究,招募了 112 名参与者,其中包括 13 至 19 岁的青少年、看护者、教师、青年领袖、社区卫生工作者、辅导员和儿童保护行动者。
elements_zh.methods: 通过深入访谈、焦点小组讨论、情绪映射、个人时间表和指导故事讲述来收集数据,并应用反思性主题分析来解释研究结果。
elements_zh.main_results: 出现了四个主题:痛苦的景观(悲伤、恐惧、与贫困有关的耻辱、学校中断)、性别和交叉的脆弱性(早婚、性暴力、教育机会差异)、应对和恢复力(信仰、同伴团结、创造性表达、愿望)以及导航支持(信任障碍、耻辱、非正式网络)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将塞拉利昂的青少年心理健康解释为由超出个人应对能力的分层、交叉危机造成的,强调需要以学校为基础的社会心理支持、社区层面的耻辱减少和促进性别平等的服务。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持优先考虑以学校为基础的社会心理支持、减少社区耻辱和促进性别平等的心理健康服务,以解决塞拉利昂危机后的青少年困扰。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 定性设计和有目的抽样限制了普遍性,缺乏定量测量或纵向随访限制了因果推断;证据强度被评估为中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 塞拉利昂的青少年经历了一系列危机,包括国内冲突、2014年至2016年的埃博拉病毒病 暴发和COVID-19大流行,每一次都加剧了心理健康、教育和家庭稳定方面本来就存在的脆弱性。尽管全球日益认识到青少年心理健康是公共卫生的优先事项,但记录塞拉利昂年轻人如何经历痛苦、应对和恢复的定性证据仍然有限。这项研究调查了塞拉利昂青少年如何经历心理健康、福祉、应对、学校教育和危机后恢复。2024 年 2 月至 7 月期间,在塞拉利昂的三个地区进行了一项定性参与性研究。针对性抽样招募了 112 名参与者,其中包括 13 至 19 岁的青少年、看护者、教师、青年领袖、社区卫生工作者、辅导员和儿童保护行动者。通过深度访谈、焦点小组讨论、情绪映射、个人时间表和引导故事讲述来收集数据。应用反思性主题分析。我们确定了四个主题:(1)痛苦景观,包括悲伤、恐惧、与贫困相关的羞耻和学校中断;(2) 性别和交叉脆弱性,包括早婚、性暴力和教育机会差异;(3) 通过信仰、同伴团结、创造性表达和愿望来应对、恢复和创造意义;(4) 引导支持,揭示信任障碍、耻辱和非正式网络的中心地位。塞拉利昂青少年的心理健康受到分层、交叉的危机的影响,这些危机超出了个人的应对能力。迫切需要以学校为基础的社会心理支持、社区层面的减少耻辱以及促进性别平等的服务。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 这项研究是必要的,因为塞拉利昂的青少年面临着分层危机——内战、2014-2016 埃博拉病毒病 暴发 和 COVID-19——这些危机加剧了心理健康、教育和家庭稳定方面本来就存在的脆弱性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024 年 2 月至 7 月期间,在塞拉利昂的三个地区进行了一项定性参与性研究,招募了 112 名参与者,其中包括 13 至 19 岁的青少年、看护者、教师、青年领袖、社区卫生工作者、辅导员和儿童保护行动者。
analysis_zh.methods: 通过深入访谈、焦点小组讨论、情绪映射、个人时间表和指导故事讲述来收集数据,并应用反思性主题分析来解释研究结果。
analysis_zh.main_results: 出现了四个主题:痛苦的景观(悲伤、恐惧、与贫困有关的耻辱、学校中断)、性别和交叉的脆弱性(早婚、性暴力、教育机会差异)、应对和恢复力(信仰、同伴团结、创造性表达、愿望)以及导航支持(信任障碍、耻辱、非正式网络)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将塞拉利昂的青少年心理健康解释为由超出个人应对能力的分层、交叉危机造成的,强调需要以学校为基础的社会心理支持、社区层面的耻辱减少和促进性别平等的服务。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果支持优先考虑以学校为基础的社会心理支持、减少社区耻辱和促进性别平等的心理健康服务,以解决塞拉利昂危机后的青少年困扰。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 定性设计和有目的抽样限制了普遍性,缺乏定量测量或纵向随访限制了因果推断;证据强度被评估为中等。
